story: Hanuman, son of the wind god Vayu and Anjana, was cursed as a child to forget his powers until someone reminded him. When Sita was taken to Lanka, the bear king Jambavan reminded him, and he leapt across the ocean, found her, and set Lanka on fire. When Lakshmana lay dying, he carried a whole mountain back to bring the healing herb.
belief: Devotees believe Hanuman is a chiranjeevi, an immortal, still present wherever Rama's name is sung. He is prayed to for strength, courage and protection, especially on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
turns: As a baby he mistook the rising sun for a ripe fruit and leapt to eat it, and Indra struck him with a thunderbolt. His mischief in the sages' hermitages is what led them to curse him to forget his strength.
facts: The Hanuman Chalisa, 40 verses by Tulsidas, is one of the most recited Hindu prayers.
'Hanu' means jaw; his name is linked to the thunderbolt that struck his jaw.
He rode on Arjuna's flag throughout the Mahabharata war.
lessons: You are stronger than you remember.
Serve with your whole heart and fear leaves.
more: He is said to have torn open his chest to show Rama and Sita living in his heart.
Hanuman Jayanti is celebrated on the full moon of Chaitra across much of India.
